capabilities: Select whole list blocks with Esc and move, extend, or delete them with the keyboard
Jump to ancestor list items and create new siblings at the end of the current level
Set task keywords like TODO and DONE on selected blocks by pressing letters
Wrap selections in bracket pairs and insert horizontal rules below blocks
Convert block types between bullet, numbered, and paragraph, and stack notes in a Logseq-like sidebar
disambiguation: Not a full Logseq-style outliner; it adds block-selection and navigation commands on top of Obsidian's normal lists.
extras: Installation is manual from Releases or via BRAT; feedback and updates are handled through the author's Twitter account. Some editor keys (Enter, Esc, arrows) have fixed bindings and cannot be rebound.
motivation: The author moved from Logseq to Obsidian and missed how Logseq treats every list item as a block that can be grabbed and moved.
problem: Obsidian lacks block-based list editing moves that Emacs-style outliners have, such as grabbing a list item with its children and jumping to the parent item.

relations.evidence: what I missed most was how Logseq treats every list item as a block
The other half of the inspiration comes from Emacs (org-mode outline editing) and Bike

summary: Outliner editing commands that select and move list blocks, jump to ancestors, group rows, set task keywords, and convert list types, inspired by Logseq and Emacs.
